sharedProposal.casting: KEEP each actual class access row, rank 4/base 7 RP, minimum class level and repertoire. All thirteen use Action and V/S/F; Summon Corpse Golem preserves V/S/M/F with the existing unpriced material-or-focus alternative. The ordinary casting engine, actual hand/voice/focus requirements, RP discounts and surcharges, Dissonance/Refrain and source hooks apply. Observable legality precedes commitment; hidden defenses or concealed ineligibility give no free diagnostic or refund. Commit the actual Action, costs and cadence before the counter window. A concentration cast displaces incompatible old concentration at commitment even if countered. Attack modifier is actual source PB plus casting modifier; save DC is 8 plus those values. Saves are binary, without natural-die degree shifts. No generic upcast, level scaling, extra turn or unacquired source is supplied.
sharedProposal.clocks: NEW for these cards, durations expressed in minutes/hours use absolute elapsed deadlines from resolution: one minute is sixty seconds and one hour is 3,600 seconds. Expiry precedes a use scheduled at exactly that deadline. A hostile one-round rider uses the first future target regular END excluding the in-progress turn; N future target-end installments use precisely N such endpoints. Outside initiative use the stated 6N seconds. Preserve the chosen virtual marker or absolute deadline through reordering, extra turns, absence, entry and exit from initiative. NEW attached-asset bridge for Mind Maze and Leeching Plague: if the recipient has only a real original-owner attached phase, use its next future attached-phase END excluding a phase already underway; if it has no real turn/phase, use six-second END-only checkpoints. Mapping a checkpoint supplies no ordinary turn, Action, death save, refresh or extra tick. Due effects run before their own ending cleanup. Suppressed scheduled installments are spent without effect; they never accumulate.
sharedProposal.identityAndMultiplicity: NEW explicit group default: one active instance per original caster per ordinary spell ID; a successfully established replacement ends only that caster’s old active instance. An invalid or countered nonconcentration cast leaves the old instance, while ordinary concentration displacement still happens at commitment. A successfully resisted cast establishes nothing and does not replace an old nonconcentration rider. Different owners keep separate source records and endpoints, with stated same-family caps and the existing strongest same-stat flat-bonus rules. Do not generalize that bonus rule into a universal strongest-effect rule. Each record retains caster, class, rank, cast ID, snapshotted spell DC, recipients/anchor, actual history and ending. Transfer, form change or a new database ID cannot rearm it. Nonconcentration voluntary dismissal here requires the original caster’s Action and perception/line of effect to the recipient or anchor within original range; completed instantaneous consequences cannot be recalled.
sharedProposal.perceptionAndIllusions: KEEP actual sight, hearing, Hidden, cover and Invisible rules. Ordinary invisibility does not hide location automatically. Once an observer knows location, it loses only Invisible-specific attack advantage/disadvantage; sight-required targeting still requires actual sight. Resolve a revealing attack first, then give location knowledge only to observers perceiving its evidence. Alternate senses work only within their real scope. NEW apply the current LR-G07 examination procedure to these new visual illusions: an Action with a relevant accessible sense permits INT (Investigation) against the creating spell’s snapshotted DC, using Core degrees/natural shifts then collapsing Success/Critical Success versus Failure/Critical Failure. Failure permits another attempt only with genuinely new evidence or method. Conclusive personally witnessed physical contradiction identifies the false part without a roll. A warning enables examination but does not globally identify the spell for everybody. Images add no actual cover, collision, support, light, sound, creature body, remote senses or inventory unless expressly supplied below. No compelled belief, automatic disguise success or knowledge of hidden terrain is granted.
sharedProposal.damageHealingAndCosts: KEEP typed damage defenses, actual prevention/sharing, buffers, life-state rules, Wounds and concentration. Save-half floors before the relevant defenses. Numeric actualDamageDealt is temporary HP absorbed plus actual normal HP lost, excluding overkill and prevented HP-floor loss. For a permitted drain sum eligible terminal recipient branches once, never both a split parent and its children; apply the card’s narrower funding predicate before its final half/floor. HP restoration uses actual healing restrictions and maximums and grants no automatic Wound cure, resurrection or resource refresh. Direct HP payment is separate from damage: no resistance, buffer, transfer, Wound/damage trigger or damage-derived refund. It must be paid from real normal HP under the card’s explicit floor. No necrotic, shadow, plague or soul name creates an unprinted condition, material, pool or setting fact.
sharedProposal.assetsAndControl: KEEP the real owner-wide one command and one offensive companion/device allowance per numbered round. Commands use the owner’s Bonus Action on their regular turn, actual audible/visible communication within sixty feet, and execute in the attached phase after that whole turn. No immediate creation movement/attack and no extra-turn refresh. An issued command survives later owner incapacity only while the actual source and other eligibility survive. Uncommanded assets can move defensively and Dodge, subject to conditions. Current owner-source PB supplies saves; specified base HP/AC remain fixed except genuinely acquired source-qualified modifiers. No borrowed monster abilities or unstated condition/damage immunity. For the two NEW summoned bodies below and Bone Cage only, full suppression of that creating source ends that body/structure immediately rather than storing an intangible replacement. Actual riders or narrowly scoped suppression still affect only their own scope. Ending drops actual cargo/riders at their actual locations with ordinary support/Falling; it creates no salvage, corpse, duplicate equipment or reappearance. This explicit NEW ending rule does not amend other summons.
sharedProposal.hardControlAndMovement: KEEP the source-character/target/encounter hard-denial allowance shared across that owner’s effects. A whole-Action/turn denial spends it only when established; resistance, immunity or an already-used allowance supplies no invented fallback. Soft Speed effects, an obstacle and a numeric attack/save penalty do not themselves spend it. Teleportation relocates without spending Speed, traversing the path or provoking ordinary opportunity attacks. Speed 0 alone is not a relocation prohibition; an actual teleport/relocation prohibition still applies. Verify whole body, actual legal cargo, occupancy and destination before resolution. Only actual carried noncreature belongings travel unless a card expressly permits passengers; another creature, grappled victim, carried living body or mount stays with its own real position/support. No route between planes, custody bypass, resource refill or returned movement budget is implied.

records.procedure: Action; range 60 feet; V/S/F. Choose one willing creature you perceive with line of effect, including yourself. KEEP the target stays Invisible while attacking. NEW replace the contradictory Instantaneous metadata with concentration up to sixty elapsed seconds. Unlike the reviewed ordinary Invisibility identity, no Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, attack, dealt damage, forced save, spellcasting or other technique ends this effect merely by being used. Actual loss of this spell’s concentration, expiry, qualifying removal or the recipient’s actual death ends it. A different concentration spell cast by its own caster still displaces it normally. The recipient’s actual initial worn/held/carried noncreature gear within its lawful anatomy and capacity shares visual concealment while that same item remains in its possession. Dropped, fired or transferred items immediately become visible; regripping one later does not restore this cast’s concealment, and newly picked-up external property never gains it. No carried creature, mount or independently living body is concealed by that gear clause. Existing melded property retains its real body/equipment history without creating a second visible item. Ordinary voice, footfalls, tracks, light emitted by actual equipment and physical interaction remain real. A revealing attack can leave the creature Invisible while observers learn its location and lose only the Invisible-specific attack modifiers. Neither location knowledge nor Investigation grants sight through this actual condition; use an actual qualifying sense/removal. Suppression suspends this record’s concealment while its original deadline runs; it neither deletes observer knowledge nor restores a spent/released item to the initial gear set. Multiple owners’ sources retain separate concentration records, with no stacked Invisible benefit. There is no continuing caster-to-target range tether after application.
records.newChoices: NEW willing recipient, sixty-second concentration and explicit no-action-ending scope, initial-only gear set, death endpoint and observer-specific information handling. The stronger printed attack exception is retained; reviewed ordinary Invisibility and Mislead stay unchanged.
workedCases: IN4-01-A: Bea receives the spell at t=0 with her worn armor and bow. She attacks at t=8; the revealing attack resolves before an observing guard learns her location. She remains Invisible, but that guard gains no continuing Invisible-specific disadvantage merely from her unseen appearance. The fired arrow becomes visible when released.

IN4-01-B: At t=20 Bea picks up a visible key; it remains visible. Full effect suppression at t=30 suspends her concealment until t=40, but the original t=60 deadline and the guard’s knowledge persist. If the original caster starts another concentration spell at t=45, this record ends even if that new spell is countered.

Define equipment/cargo and transfer boundaries, application replacement and suppression without creating silence, automatic Hide, incorporeality or indiscriminate immunity to targeting. explicitJointIssues: Greater Invisibility proposes the full action/attack exemption and willing target at sixty feet, while retaining the native observer-specific location rules. Compare the now-reviewed ordinary Invisibility and Mislead records, not stale preparation labels.

Hallucinatory Terrain interprets 150 feet as both casting range and maximum horizontal span, with a thirty-foot vertical limit and one-hour concentration. Terrain appearance cannot conceal creatures or remove real occlusion. Confirm this finite utility and overlap rule.

Mind Maze is a custom whole-round denial under the existing shared hard guard. It does not silently become Stunned/Incapacitated or end concentration; its attached-phase bridge and committed-action handling need exact review.

Illusory Clone proposes a visual image with bounded mirrored translation and an own-turn Bonus Action swap. Its once-per-round ledger survives recast and extra turns; it is neither Mirror Image defense nor Mislead invisibility.

Greater Phantom Steed proposes three fixed alternative specialties and one-hour concentration. Review flight, weight/Load, real control/travel and the contrast with the lesser nonconcentration steed; none certifies transport balance.

Shadow Step keeps Action/sixty feet and requires actual darkness at both ends plus independent destination perception. The same-named Monk/Oracle techniques retain their separate gates, costs and riders.

Corpse Golem proposes a temporary construct without a real corpse input, retaining HP 60 and 2d10. Its slow aura is a separately commanded offensive alternative to Slam, with bounded duration and CON/half-Speed membership. Confirm this deliberate action-economy completion.

Leeching Plague proposes CON-negates application, four future-END damage opportunities, no concentration and restricted numeric actual-damage healing. Buffers can fund its heal; this intentionally differs from Soul Tap’s normal-HP-only transaction and preserves all older spell predicates.

Aura of Dread proposes a no-save minute concentration aura for the printed flat -1. It affects attacks and saves only, grants no fear/hidden-intent readout and duplicates do not sum. Confirm its interaction with genuinely independent penalty sources.

Soulburn Pact has a literal current 3-RP versus Core 5-RP conflict and a retained 7-RP base price. This proposal selects up to three without concealing its negative resource yield, adds a one-use beneficial-rest limit and pays twenty normal HP before countering. The amount, utility and added frequency are material joint design decisions.

Blight’s plant enhancement is explicitly +2d8 with the same CON half save, not maximization, disadvantage or automatic death. Mundane plant targeting needs actual finite identity/durability and grants no free harvest.

Shadow of Moil retains broad resistance to all damage with cosmetic-only shadows, minute concentration and native defense ordering. Broad mitigation is a material balance issue; no external retaliation or darkness rule is imported.

Bone Cage proposes a finite breakable object with DEX-negates formation and half cover, preserving target actions and ordinary relocation. Confirm whole-frame placement, three-inch gaps and the ten-foot-face opening procedure.

The proposed full-source-suppression ending for these two summons and Bone Cage is explicitly NEW and local to this cohort. It drops actual supported bodies/cargo normally and cannot retroactively change the handling of any previously reviewed summon.

preparedCompleteRecord.name: Mirror Image

operational.targets: Self; creates 3 illusory duplicates occupying your space and moving with you
operational.duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute or until all 3 duplicates are destroyed
operational.resolution: When an attack roll directly targets you, randomly select among you and all remaining duplicates with equal probability before the attack roll. If you are selected, resolve the attack against you normally. If a duplicate is selected, resolve the attack roll against your current AC; on a hit that duplicate is destroyed, and on a miss it remains. Area effects ignore the duplicates.
operational.effect: Create three illusory duplicates of yourself. Direct attack rolls may strike a duplicate instead of you until the duplicates are destroyed or concentration ends.
operational.limitations: Duplicates have no Actions, HP, independent positions, attacks, bodies, cover, collision, resource triggers, or ability to intercept saving-throw effects. They cannot be deliberately targeted by you or allies to generate procs. A creature that does not rely on sight or explicitly ignores visual illusions targets you normally. Ranked casting causes normal Dissonance and Refrain.
operational.designNotes: The two Core V2 entries conflict: one gives 30-foot range and concentration up to 1 minute, while the other gives Self and Instantaneous. Because the source consistently says duplicates of yourself, this pilot uses self range and retains the coherent 1-minute concentration duration. V/S/M/F is represented as a small reflective token or existing class casting focus. Equal random selection and duplicate-hit procedure are NEW provisional mechanics.

preparedCompleteRecord.name: Summon Lesser Skeleton

operational.targets: One unoccupied space you can perceive within range; summons one Lesser Skeleton companion
operational.duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute
operational.resolution: No initial roll. The skeleton's commanded melee attack uses your spell attack bonus.
operational.effect: Summon one Lesser Skeleton with AC 13, 10 HP, Speed 30 feet, saves equal to your PB, other checks +0, and one melee attack with 5-foot reach that deals 1d6 bludgeoning, piercing or slashing damage (choose one type on casting and keep it fixed for that summon) on a hit. It acts immediately after you. While within 60 feet and able to perceive your command, it may be commanded with your Bonus Action to move and take its one attack or another basic action; without a command it may move and Dodge.
operational.scaling: None for source-specific AC, HP, and attack die; AC remains 13, HP remains 10, and damage remains 1d6.
operational.limitations: All companions you control share one Bonus Action command and one damaging companion action total per round. The skeleton has no unstated resistances, immunities, multiattack, spellcasting, loot, XP, resource generation, death trigger, corpse-proc eligibility, or free healing. It disappears at 0 HP or when concentration ends. Recasting replaces your prior Lesser Skeleton from this spell. Ranked casting causes normal Dissonance and Refrain.
operational.designNotes: Core V2 Action, 30-foot range, concentration up to 1 minute, and V/S/F components are retained. Source-specific AC 13, HP 10, and 1d6 melee override generic companion values. Speed, saves, checks, attack bonus, command economy, and anti-loop restrictions are NEW provisional specifications required by the shared summon interface. Conference decision: unspecified source melee damage gets a choice of bludgeoning, piercing or slashing, fixed when summoned; this is explicitly provisional.

preparedCompleteRecord.name: Summon Earth Pet

operational.targets: One unoccupied space you perceive within range and line of effect.
operational.duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute. In initiative, expires at the caster's tenth future regular-start marker after application; preserve the virtual phase through initiative changes, absence, death and planar travel. Outside initiative, expires 60 seconds after application, retaining that absolute deadline when entering initiative. An already-passed start does not count. Ends earlier at concentration end or pet 0 HP.
operational.resolution: No initial roll. Its commanded offensive Action makes one melee spell attack using your actual casting-class spell attack bonus, reach 5 feet. A hit deals 1d10 bludgeoning, with no ability damage modifier. After that hit, a Large-or-smaller target makes a Strength save against your spell DC; failure makes it Prone. A successful save prevents only knockdown. Ordinary attack, critical and defense rules apply.
operational.effect: Summon one Medium earth elemental companion: AC 17, HP 30, walking Speed30, body mass 300 pounds, saves equal to owner PB, other checks +0, ordinary sight/hearing. It understands your spoken commands but has no speaking language or telepathy. It acts immediately after you. Your Bonus Action, while within 60 feet and able to convey a perceived command, permits movement plus its attack or one basic legal nondamaging Action. Without a command it may move defensively and Dodge. The attack consumes the owner-wide one offensive companion Action for that numbered round even on a miss; it shares the owner-wide command allowance.
operational.scaling: Only the printed owner PB saves and actual class spell attack/DC change with the caster. AC 17, HP 30, 1d10 damage and one attack remain fixed; no standard S-dice progression.
operational.limitations: Huge/Gargantuan targets take damage normally but are ineligible for this knockdown unless an exact rule overrides that size gate. Prone immunity or an exact immunity expressly covering knockdown prevents Prone; immunity only to positional push/pull does not itself grant Prone immunity. Damage reduced to 0 does not erase a resolved hit or its separate save. Knockdown supplies no displacement, collision damage, stun or whole-Action denial; ordinary support/Falling and stand-up rules apply. One Earth Pet per caster; it vanishes at 0 HP or concentration end. No burrow, tremorsense, earth glide, resistance, immunity, hands/tool use, cargo capacity, free Help advantage, autonomous opportunity attack, spellcasting, loot, corpse or resource/death trigger. Its printed mass is real for carrying and condition accounting but cannot be harvested as permanent stone. A successful replacement has its own endpoint; stale cleanup cannot end the new application. A countered cast creates no replacement, although its concentration transition has already occurred. Actual class access, rank, preparation, V/S/F components, casting costs, Dissonance/Refrain, class hooks, concentration transitions and counter windows follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. Costs and beginning hooks commit before interruption, with no refunds or restoration of prior concentration. Direct target selection and local creation require the printed line of effect; expressly remote teleport destinations use their own printed rules. No generic upcast or unstated scaling.
operational.designNotes: PRESERVED: Action/60 feet/V,S,F/concentration 1 minute, AC 17/HP 30/1d10 bludgeoning plus knockdown. NEW: Medium/300 lb/Speed30, finite companion interface, spell attack and STR-save knockdown capped at Large. Exact-card clarification distinguishes positional forced-movement immunity from an explicit knockdown/Prone immunity.
operational.implementationStatus: REVIEWED authored operational-playtest manuscript; runtime, travel-system implementation, numerical balance and whole-game validation pending

preparedCompleteRecord.name: Resonance Well

operational.targets: One fixed point you can perceive within range and line of effect for a nonphysical pool of resonance.
operational.duration: If applied in initiative, expires at the caster's tenth future regular-start marker after application; preserve that virtual phase through initiative changes, absence or death. Outside initiative, expires 60 seconds after application; retain that absolute deadline on entering initiative. An already-passed start never counts. Ends earlier if the spell is ended or a later successful allowed application replaces it.
operational.resolution: Before activation/payment confirm the caster's unused character-wide Resonance Well creation use. Spend it at legal cast start before the Counterspell window. On successful resolution roll 1d4 exactly once to establish the total RP reserve. This amount belongs to the entire Well, not each recipient.
operational.effect: One creation use per character across classes/copies refreshes only at that character's actual beneficial completed long rest. A countered cast spends the use and creates no Well. A creature with an actual RP pool, including the caster, can spend an Action within 5 feet and line of effect to draw. Verify its unused character-wide Resonance Well receipt use since its own last beneficial completed long rest and a positive remaining reserve. At draw start choose a positive amount no greater than that reserve, spend the recipient use and Action, and subtract that amount immediately. At resolution restore the chosen amount, capped at actual RP maximum. Over-cap recovery is wasted; a full recipient can deliberately spend a positive draw and recover 0. Zero draw is illegal. A preventing interrupt refunds nothing.
operational.limitations: One Well per caster. Receipt use is shared across all Wells/casters/classes and refreshes only at the recipient's own beneficial long rest; creation and receipt are separate records, including when caster draws from their own Well. Kindle and Mod Rod keep their separate named ledgers: Well neither resets nor shares them. At reserve 0 the Well is inert until its endpoint. Re-entry, suppression, replacement, dispelling, copying or recovery prevention never rerolls/refills the reserve or restores spent uses. Suppression prevents drawing while applicable and does not pause duration; if drawing was already committed, a subsequent actual prevention leaves its amount/use spent. This fixed nonphysical resonance cannot be carried as water, harvested, sold, used as Supply, drawn at range or treated as a pooled RP maximum. It provides no physical support, hazard or damage despite the historical Damage tag. A successful new application owns its own endpoint; stale cleanup of a prior application cannot end its replacement. A countered cast creates no replacement. Starting concentration still ends the caster's incompatible prior concentration before interruption. Known/prepared access, actual class rank/level, V/S/F components, line of effect, costs, concentration transitions, Dissonance/Refrain, class hooks and interruption follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. Total cover blocks originating line of effect and direct targeting. No generic upcast or unstated scaling.
operational.designNotes: PRESERVED: Action/30 feet/V/S/F and a pool from which allies draw 1d4 RP. CONFLICT RULING: finite 1-minute nonconcentration pool replaces Instantaneous metadata; Damage tag grants no unprinted damage. NEW: one rolled total reserve, explicit Action/5-foot draw, caster inclusion, positive committed withdrawals and distinct creation/receipt limits per beneficial long rest. Source supplied no daily limit; both anti-farm limits are explicitly provisional additions, not recovered canon.
operational.implementationStatus: REVIEWED authored operational-playtest manuscript; runtime, CR certification and numerical balance pending

preparedCompleteRecord.name: Resonance Conduit

operational.targets: Two distinct willing creatures with actual RP pools, each perceived within 60 feet and line of effect. You may be one participant. Each participant must be free of another active Resonance Conduit.
operational.duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute. In initiative, expires at the caster's tenth future regular-start marker after application; preserve the virtual phase through initiative changes, absence, death and planar travel. Outside initiative, expires 60 seconds after application, retaining that absolute deadline when entering initiative. An already-passed start does not count. Ends earlier with concentration or either participant willingly ending the link.
operational.resolution: Automatic link creation, no RP transfer from the casting itself. Either participant may spend an Action to transfer a positive integer of existing RP to the other while both are on the same plane, within 60 feet of one another and have line of effect. At transfer start the recipient must accept; choose an amount no greater than donor currentRP or recipient currently missingRP. Commit the Action and immediately deduct that amount from the donor. At resolution credit the same amount, capped at recipient actual maximumRP; any newly excess amount is lost.
operational.effect: The two creatures retain separate RP pools and maxima. Deducted pendingRP is not spendable by either party and cannot be committed again; only a completed credit enters the recipient's pool. At resolution the link and recipient acceptance must still exist and same-plane/range/line-of-effect gates must still hold. If an exact interrupt or loss of these conditions prevents the transfer after commitment, its RP and Action are not refunded. Ordinary movement outside the transfer gate suspends permission without ending the link or pausing duration; returning restores only future permission. Either participant may voluntarily end the whole link without an Action, including before agreeing to a new conduit; ending one participant's link releases both, but never reverses completed or committed transfers. The caster can maintain only one conduit and each participant can belong to only one at a time.
operational.limitations: The original cast pays its own 5 RP base cost and applicable surcharges before the link exists; future transfer cannot finance it retroactively. Transferring is not casting, recovery from rest or creation of RP. Casting/Dissonance/Refrain/resource-generation hooks do not apply unless an exact feature expressly names Conduit transfer. No joint maximum, discounts on the transfer amount, overflow store, negative balance, duplicate credits, borrowed casting rights, simultaneous double spending, future recovery, HP, charges or materials. Copies cannot duplicate transfers or create spendable RP. No daily limit is added; named recovery ledgers, Dissonance, Refrain, actions and clocks remain unchanged. Suppression prevents transfer while applicable without pausing the endpoint; it never refunds a committed transfer. Renewed consent alone cannot revive an ended application. A later legal casting may create a new Resonance Conduit normally, paying all costs and establishing a new application and endpoint. A successful replacement has its own endpoint; stale cleanup cannot end the new application. A countered cast creates no replacement, although its concentration transition has already occurred. Actual class access, rank, preparation, V/S/F components, casting costs, Dissonance/Refrain, class hooks, concentration transitions and counter windows follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. Costs and beginning hooks commit before interruption, with no refunds or restoration of prior concentration. Direct target selection and local creation require the printed line of effect; expressly remote teleport destinations use their own printed rules. No generic upcast or unstated scaling.
operational.designNotes: PRESERVED: Action/60 feet/V,S,F and RP sharing between allies. CONFLICT RULING: Core Instantaneous metadata becomes a NEW finite 1 minute concentration permission rather than an indefinite shared pool. NEW: two participants/one link each, Action transfer, actual-pool conservation,60 foot same-plane/line-of-effect gate, commitment/no-refund timing, current-cap clipping and explicit participant withdrawal.
operational.implementationStatus: REVIEWED authored operational-playtest manuscript; runtime, travel-system implementation, numerical balance and whole-game validation pending

operational.targets: One creature you perceive within30feet and line of effect. Choose Ease or Burden at casting; Ease requires actual willingness at application.
operational.duration: Until the next qualifying spell commits or up to1minute, no concentration. In initiative, expires at the caster's tenth future regular-start marker after application; an already-passed start never counts. Outside initiative, expires after 60 elapsed seconds. Retain the original virtual phase or absolute deadline through initiative changes, absence and planar travel; moving between timing modes does not reset it.
operational.resolution: Ease: automatic on a willing target; establish a pending−1RP final-price modifier. Burden: target makes a Wisdom save even if willing unless an independent rule grants a save waiver; failure establishes pending+1RP, success creates no replacement. One pending Resonance Influence record per target across casters; a successful eligible application replaces the previous mode/deadline. Invalid or saved-against application does not erase a valid old record.
operational.effect: For the target’s next actual spell cast whose procedure has an RP-price interface, compute the ordinary legal RP price first: actual class/source rank/base, mandatory printed spell extras, applicable Dissonance surcharge, and only the exact eligible class/source reductions or waivers with their scopes/minimums. Then apply this spell’s final±1, minimum0, with no credit/refund. An ordinary0RP cantrip qualifies: Burden prices it at1; Ease leaves it0 and is still consumed. A genuine RP-priced spell reduced/waived to0 also qualifies; this final modifier can make its payment1. A charge-only item spell or free technique with no RP-price interface does not qualify and consumes nothing. An RP-priced actual class/item spell can qualify; paying RP for a nonspell technique alone does not. Validate adjusted affordability and all other preflight rules, then consume the record atomically at legal cast commitment with payment. Later failure/countering does not refund the rider. An illegal/unaffordable attempted cast never commits and leaves it available.
operational.scaling: None. No automatic increase in range, targets, duration, magnitude or uses.
operational.limitations: Ready pays/consumes at spell preparation, not release. This new application cannot retroactively alter its own already-paid casting price; a previously existing Influence may price that cast normally. Ordinary class minimums govern their own discount calculations first; the final Ease may then reduce an otherwise1RP result to0. Mandatory extras remain in that ordinary price, not omitted, though Ease can offset1RP of the resulting total. Other non-RP costs, charges, limited uses, rank/access/repertoire, components, Fractured restriction, Dissonance and Refrain are unchanged. A pending hostile+1 requires real adjusted affordability but does not grant the caster hidden knowledge of RP pools or pricing failures. Current quote_cast helper lacks this stateful modifier and class-discount integration; this card is a tabletop interface, not a runtime implementation. Actual class access/repertoire, costs, components, Dissonance/Refrain, concentration transitions and cast/counter order follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. Pay a legal cast before effect resolution; failure/countering refunds nothing and restores no displaced concentration. V is audible, S requires the ordinary usable hand, and F is the normal class focus. Saves use the actual casting class's spell DC and binary save rules. Creature type alone supplies no mental immunity; Charmed-only immunity does not block effects that never impose Charmed. Actual broader defenses retain their written scope. No automatic scaling, generic upcast or free identification of hidden eligibility.
operational.designNotes: PRESERVED: Action/30feet/V,S,F and next-spell RP cost±1. NEW: modes, willingness/WIS, minute, final-price ordering, replacement and cast-commit consumption. Exact-review proposal explicitly includes a normally RP-priced cast made free by another source, while excluding a source with no RP-price interface; final modifier follows source-specific minimum calculations.

preparedCompleteRecord.name: Slow

operational.targets: Actual Enchantment mode: choose up to six creatures you perceive within 60 feet and line of effect. Actual Transmutation mode: the triggering creature must be perceived within 60 feet and line of effect and must be selected; choose up to five additional such creatures. The actual casting class determines school/mode; paying the same rank-3/base-5-RP price never grants the other package.
operational.duration: Both modes: concentration, up to one minute. In initiative, the maximum ends at the caster's tenth future regular-turn START after application, excluding any start already underway/passed. If begun outside initiative, the maximum is 60 elapsed seconds. Preserve the original virtual marker/absolute deadline through initiative changes, extra turns, absence and planar travel; no timing-mode change resets it.
operational.resolution: Enchantment uses an Action and an independent Wisdom save per target. Transmutation uses a Reaction when a creature you perceive within 60 feet/line of effect begins a distinct voluntary movement segment or begins an Action on its own actual turn, after required declaration/commitment and before the segment’s first step or Action’s first main outcome. An extra turn can trigger; Bonus Actions and Reactions cannot. Transmutation gives each chosen target an independent Constitution save. Success: no new effect for that target. Failure: apply only that actual mode’s independently defended rider set. Each affected creature repeats that mode’s recorded WIS or CON save at every affected regular-turn END, including the current regular turn if applied during it; success ends that cast’s application on that creature. Extra turns grant no ending saves. Outside initiative an otherwise legally established ongoing effect uses the specifically bound six-second END-save cadence, never a new Reaction trigger.
operational.effect: Enchantment failure: half Speed under existing strongest-adverse-Speed arbitration; -2 AC; -2 Dexterity ability checks and Dexterity saving throws, expressly excluding initiative; and at most one full Action commitment per actual turn. It changes no DEX score/modifier, DEX attack/damage, spell DC or other unnamed derived statistic. AC has only its separate -2. Count an Action already committed before application toward the ceiling; an already-legally-committed second Action still finishes, but no further Action can be committed that turn. The ceiling applies independently on extra turns; it retains Bonus Actions, Reactions and inherent attacks in a legal Attack Action. Transmutation failure: half Speed, -2 AC and no future Reaction commitments. It imposes no DEX penalty or Action ceiling. Already-committed unresolved Reactions remain on the LIFO stack. Neither mode grants unprinted spell delay, attack-count restriction, Action/Bonus-Action interchange, cancellation or teleport restriction.
operational.scaling: None. No automatic increase in range, targets, duration, magnitude or uses.
operational.limitations: Transmutation’s movement trigger is one distinct segment, such as moving, performing an Action, then resuming movement; choosing another square during continuous movement is not a new segment, and individual feet/tiles are never new triggers. A paid Slow remains independent if a legal nested interruption removes the original parent Action: resolve it against still-legal selected targets, without refund, revival or parent cancellation. A surviving parent Action continues after the interrupt stack; movement recalculates remaining legal allowance before the next expenditure, keeping all movement already spent. The one-Action ceiling, Reaction denial and other soft riders do not claim whole-Action hard-control allowance. Actual narrowly scoped defenses can suppress individual components. preparedCompleteRecord.name: Warding Bond

operational.targets: One willing ally other than yourself, perceived within range and line of effect. Neither participant may already participate in another Warding Bond, as caster or protected ally.
operational.duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute. In initiative, expires at the caster's tenth future regular-start marker after application; retain that virtual marker through initiative changes, departure or death. Outside initiative, expires 60 seconds after application; entering initiative preserves that absolute deadline. An already-passed start never counts. Ends earlier when concentration ends. Also ends if either participant dies. Reaching 0 HP alone is not a separate ending condition; ordinary Incapacitated/concentration rules still apply.
operational.resolution: Automatic on legal casting. On each eligible positive incoming damage packet to the ally, apply the mandatory post-defense transfer described below; a rounded-zero transfer claims no transfer operation.
operational.effect: The ally gains +1 AC and +1 to saves, subject separately to the strongest applicable flat bonus. After the ally's defenses and legal prevention, before temporary HP, transfer floor(remaining damage / 2) to you and leave the remainder on the ally. Keep the damage type. Your transferred share skips a second mitigation/prevention stage and cannot transfer again; apply your temporary HP, HP, applicable life-state protections, Wounds and concentration consequences normally. The ally retains the hit, failed-save, critical and attached-rider identity; you were not hit and did not fail that save merely because damage transferred.
operational.scaling: None. The rank-2 duplicate grants no upgrade or extra effect.
operational.limitations: Use DAMAGE_SHARING_PLAYTEST.md: one transfer operation per original-recipient damage root, across all owners. A prior pre-mitigation split preempts this transfer; competing positive mandatory post-defense claims are chosen by the original target. The retained ally portion cannot subsequently be transferred again after this split. Complete the current packet's split and life consequences before concentration failure caused by that packet ends the bond; never undo a committed share. One Warding Bond per participating creature across all casters; casting cannot create chains or cycles. Initial range/line of effect are required, but no continuing distance or line-of-effect tether is imposed. This ordinary spell neither consumes nor increases the Paladin class redirection round ledger and grants none of its named healing/resource riders or proc permissions. Unrelated downstream triggers still require their own exact source authorization. Direct HP payments are not damage and cannot be transferred. Known/prepared access, class-level gates, legal components, line of effect, payment before resolution, concentration transitions, Dissonance, Refrain and class cadence follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. No automatic scaling or generic upcast.
operational.designNotes: PRESERVED: Action, 30 feet, concentration 1 minute, +1 AC/saves and half-damage sharing; M/F uses focus. NEW: willing ally, conserved mandatory post-defense split, rounding, participation and life endpoints, no continued tether and ordinary-spell/class-engine separation. CONFLICT RULING: source-derived class access is rank 1; duplicate rank-2 block is retained as evidence only.

The rider ends at the target’s first future regular-turn END, excluding its entire current turn if already underway. Outside initiative it ends six elapsed seconds after application. Preserve the original regular/virtual marker or outside absolute deadline through initiative changes, extra turns, absence and travel; end-phase events precede expiry cleanup.
operational.resolution: Make one melee spell attack. Miss: no damage or restriction. Hit: deal 1d8 necrotic and establish the independent HP-gain prohibition under its actual defenses.
operational.effect: While affected, any event increasing the target’s current HP produces 0 gain: spell/feature/potion healing, passive regeneration, natural recovery, natural-20 death-save 1HP, Stable-state 1HP and other direct restoration. Apply HEALING_DEATH_PLAYTEST.md: ordinary healing’s legal amount and genuine excess become0; ordinary activation costs remain committed, while a reserve spent only for actual restored HP spends0. Independent non-HP components still resolve. A blocked natural20 uses the already-reviewed bridge: Stable at0, death counters cleared, immediate d4-hour recovery deadline and preserved used-turn marker. A due Stable1HP recovery remains subject to its existing blocked-deadline procedure; this spell never rerolls or resets that deadline.
operational.scaling: None. No automatic increase in damage, range, target count, duration, uses or magnitude.
operational.limitations: No Undead/biological target prerequisite or special Undead rider. The prohibition does not itself block stabilization, successful death-save state changes, temporary HP, condition removal, damage prevention, maximum-HP changes or independent non-HP components. A maximum-HP change does not authorize a separate current-HP increase through this prohibition. Actual resurrection returned HP is the existing LIFE TRANSITION exception and is not blocked; no corpse/soul/resurrection seal is created. Actual death/condition-removal procedures retain their scope, without duplicating an identity or refreshing spent resources. This is an HP-state rule, not a cosmology ruling. A hit establishes the independent rider under its own defenses even if the damage is reduced to 0; immunity to the damage type alone does not prevent that rider. A later independent application retains its own endpoint; ending one removes only that application, and equal penalties/prohibitions do not stack magnitude. Actual class/source access, repertoire, action availability, components, RP, Dissonance/Refrain, concentration transitions, paid commitment and cast/counter/outcome hooks follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. Base rank 0 costs 0 RP but does not waive real extra costs or Refrain. V requires audible speech; S requires the ordinary usable free hand or an actual exception. No F is added. Spell attacks use d20 + PB + actual casting modifier against AC; natural 1 misses, natural 20 hits and doubles only actual damage dice. Saves use DC 8 + PB + actual casting modifier and binary-save rules. An illegal uncommitted attempt supplies no effect; a legally paid cast countered or failing afterward refunds nothing. Actual damage/material/condition defenses retain their own scopes. No automatic level scaling, extra action budget or resource generation.
operational.designNotes: PRESERVED: both Evocation/Necromancy sources and actual access, Action, Touch, V/S, 1d8 necrotic and cannot regain HP. NEW: melee spell attack, hit-based independent broad current-HP-gain prohibition, explicit future-target-END duration, state-recovery bindings and existing resurrection life-transition boundary. completeCurrentEnvelope.protectedInterfaceOriginal: Once per turn, spending 2 or more Conviction on a Rite or Invocation vents 1 Dissonance; prayer changes cadence instead of bypassing Resonance.
engine: PROVISIONAL PLAYTEST CONTRACT. Wisdom is the Cleric class ability. S = 1/2/3/4 at Cleric levels 1/5/11/17. M = max(1, Wisdom modifier) unless a feature explicitly substitutes another ability. Cleric technique attack = d20 + normal character proficiency bonus + Wisdom modifier. Cleric technique save DC = 8 + normal character proficiency bonus + Wisdom modifier.

Conviction is separate from Resonance Points. Base Conviction maximum is 3, automatically becoming 5 at Cleric 9; after a long rest you begin at your current maximum. A completed short rest restores 1 spent Conviction, to the maximum. A completed long rest restores all Conviction. Conviction Pool raises the maximum by 2. Conviction persists between encounters; simply declaring prayer, repeating a Rite, or performing harmless actions outside a real encounter never generates Conviction.

Only explicit features generate Conviction. Sacred Chant, Sermon of Purpose, Doctrine Shield, Dark Conviction and other printed cards are valid generators. A feature cannot generate more Conviction than its text permits, and Conviction can never exceed the current maximum. Summoned creatures, friendly creatures, trivial creatures, repeated corpse manipulation and staged out-of-combat actions cannot be used to farm Conviction.

Cleric techniques use only their printed RP and Conviction costs. All RP is paid from the Cleric's Core Systems V 2 Resonance Point pool. A Cleric technique is not automatically an ordinary spell-rank cast and does not receive Overcast, spell-slot, cost-discount or spell-proc benefits unless a feature explicitly says otherwise. Ordinary spells continue to use Core V 2 spellcasting rules.

Protected Dissonance interaction: once on each of your regular turns, when you spend at least 2 Conviction on a Rite or Invocation, reduce Dissonance by 1, minimum 0. The expenditure must actually occur; waived Conviction costs do not vent Dissonance. A single feature expenditure vents at most once even if it spends more than 2 Conviction. No Cleric card automatically adds Dissonance unless explicitly written.

One concentration effect may be maintained at a time. Starting another concentration effect immediately ends the previous one. Damage uses the current Core Systems concentration rule; for this pilot, if a division requires rounding, half damage is rounded down. Sustained Cleric effects use their printed maintenance cost and Bonus Action. A control effect that persists for multiple pulses or rounds gives the target a new save at each printed pulse or at the end of each affected turn as stated.

Round recharge counters are set after resolution and decrease once at the start of the Cleric's regular initiative turn, even if the Cleric cannot act. Extra Actions and extra turns do not create extra recharge ticks. Outside initiative, each uninterrupted 6 seconds counts as one recharge tick. Only a positive counter may be reset or shortened, and a named ability can receive at most one reset or shortening per round.

Healing cannot exceed maximum HP, does not remove Wounds, and does not restore a dead creature unless a card explicitly says it resurrects. No Cleric feature provides unlimited permanent HP or resource restoration outside encounters. Temporary HP does not stack with itself; use the higher value. Resurrection and corpse-based effects have explicit use limits and cannot generate repeatable corpses, XP, loot or Conviction.

Invocation Attunement is gained automatically at Cleric level 2. Choose exactly one Invocation Path: Radiance, Judgment, Renewal, Flame, Veil or Echoes. Only the selected path bonus becomes active. Divine Invocation uses the mode belonging to that selected path unless another feature explicitly permits a different mode. Changing Invocation Path requires a future explicit retraining rule; this draft provides none.

PROPOSED ACQUISITION FOR PLAYTEST. Cleric 1: gain the Divine Favor engine and choose 4 Base cards, at least 2 Active. Cleric 2: automatically gain Invocation Attunement and the selected Invocation Path bonus, then choose 2 additional Base cards. Cleric 3: enter Bishop and choose 2 Arch cards, at least 1 Active. Levels 4-8 each grant one eligible Base/Arch choice, respecting each card's minimum class level. Level 9 grants one eligible Arch choice plus Bishop's Mandate automatically. Level 10 choose Saint, Priest or Cultist and gain 2 Hero choices from that path. Levels 12, 14, 16 and 18 each grant one additional Hero choice; levels 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19 grant one eligible unselected Base/Arch choice. The chosen Hero Finale is automatic at Cleric 20. ASI/feat milestones remain separate and do not consume these choices.

All acquisition gates use Cleric class level, not total character level. Proficiency bonus still follows normal total-character-level rules. A multiclass character cannot use non-Cleric levels to unlock Bishop, Hero, Invocation or Finale features. Divine commands, visions and social abilities can influence actions only to the extent their exact mechanical text states; no Cleric feature can force a player character to adopt, abandon or profess a belief.

Capacity clarification: the automatic level 9 Conviction increase is a new draft completion so every Hero can pay its 5-Conviction Finale without buying Conviction Pool. Conviction Pool adds 2 at any level, yielding 5 early or 7 from 9. It never fills gained capacity immediately.
workedExample: Cleric 5 example: Wisdom 16 gives M=3, PB=3, S=2. Assume the Core V 2 sheet gives this test Cleric 12 RP. The Cleric knows Conviction Pool, so maximum Conviction is 5, begins the encounter at Conviction 5, Dissonance 3, and selected Judgment at level 2.

Turn 1: Divine Smite costs 1 Conviction, so Conviction 5→4 and RP remains 12. On a hit it deals 2d8+3 radiant damage. Judgment automatically marks the target Judged for 2 rounds, giving it -1 AC. Spending only 1 Conviction does not vent Dissonance.

Turn 2: Divine Invocation costs 2 Conviction and 3 RP, so Conviction 4→2 and RP 12→9. Because an Invocation spent at least 2 Conviction, Dissonance vents once, 3→2. Using Judgment mode, a failed Wisdom save causes the printed 3d8 radiant effect and refreshes Judged.

Turn 3: Healing Rite costs 2 RP, so RP 9→7. It restores 2d8+3 HP to one living ally. It spends no Conviction, so Conviction remains 2 and Dissonance remains 2. If the ally stood in the Cleric's Consecrate zone and Consecrated Ground was known, the target would also regain the printed S=2 bonus HP.
Turn 4: Sacred Chant costs 1 RP to start, so RP 7→6. Its first pulse occurs, but generates no Conviction yet. The Cleric concentrates on the Chant. Conviction stays 2.

Turn 5: The Cleric maintains Sacred Chant with a Bonus Action. Because Sermon of Purpose is known, the second pulse generates 1 Conviction, 2→3. The Cleric then uses Divine Smite as the normal Action, spending 1 Conviction, 3→2. RP remains 6 and Dissonance remains 2 because no single Rite or Invocation expenditure of at least 2 Conviction occurred this turn.
balanceQuestions: Does a 3-point base Conviction cap, or 5 with Conviction Pool, create meaningful expenditure choices without making Sacred Chant mandatory in every encounter?
Do Bishop's Mandate, Miraculous Channel and the six Invocation modes create excessive burst or action compression when combined, especially at levels 7-10?

Across Saint, Priest and Cultist, are healing, control, resurrection and Conviction regeneration sufficiently bounded across multiple encounters without making ordinary Core V2 spellcasting irrelevant?

cards.name: Conviction Pool
cards.effect: Conviction Pool. Tags: conviction, passive. Increase your Conviction maximum by 2. This changes only the maximum; it does not immediately restore spent Conviction when acquired during play. A long rest restores Conviction to the new maximum.

source.originalText: Conviction Pool: +2 max Conviction cap.

cards.name: Consecrated Ground
cards.effect: Consecrated Ground. Tags: rite, healing, passive. Whenever one of your healing Rites restores HP to a living creature standing in terrain created by your Consecrate feature, that creature regains S additional HP. Apply this once per creature per Rite pulse; it is flat healing and is not itself another healing trigger.

source.originalText: Consecrated Ground: Healing allies on terrain you sanctify (via Rite) heals for +10%.

cards.name: Judging Light
cards.effect: Judging Light. Tags: smite, passive. When your Divine Smite damages a creature currently affected by a Cursed or Weakened condition, add S d4 radiant damage to that Smite. Roll these dice once as part of the Smite; they do not create a second hit or trigger.

source.originalText: Judging Light: Smite deals +20% bonus damage to enemies afflicted by Cursed or Weakened effects.

cards.name: Fervent Ritualist
cards.effect: Fervent Ritualist. Tags: rite, ritual, passive. When a Rite with a Ritual activation normally requires at least 10 minutes, reduce its required time by 1 minute for each full 10 minutes of its printed casting time. This never reduces a Ritual below 1 minute and does not alter Action, Bonus Action or Reaction Rites.

source.originalText: Fervent Ritualist: +10% faster channel speed on all Rites.

cards.name: Invocation Attunement
cards.effect: Invocation Attunement. Tags: invocation, core. At Cleric level 2 choose exactly one Invocation Path: Radiance, Judgment, Renewal, Flame, Veil or Echoes. You automatically gain that path's listed bonus. Divine Invocation thereafter uses that path's mode unless another feature explicitly overrides it.

source.originalText: Invocation Attunement: Choose one Invocation Path (see below); gain a permanent passive tied to it.

cards.name: Radiance
cards.frequency: Automatic only if Radiance was selected
cards.effect: Invocation Path — Radiance. Tags: invocation, radiance, healing. Once on each of your turns when one of your Rites restores HP to at least one living creature, choose one creature healed by that Rite. It regains S additional HP and may immediately end either Frightened or Poisoned on itself.

source.originalText: Radiance: +10% healing power and heals cleanse minor conditions.

cards.name: Judgment
cards.frequency: Automatic only if Judgment was selected
cards.effect: Invocation Path — Judgment. Tags: invocation, judgment, smite. When your Divine Smite deals damage to a creature, mark it Judged for 2 rounds. A Judged creature has -1 AC. Further applications refresh the duration but do not increase the AC penalty.

source.originalText: Judgment: Smites mark enemies with Judged for 2 rounds, reducing their AC by 1.

cards.name: Renewal
cards.frequency: Automatic only if Renewal was selected
cards.effect: Invocation Path — Renewal. Tags: invocation, renewal, healing, rite. Once per use of a healing Rite, choose one creature that actually regained HP from it. That creature also restores 5 Stamina, not exceeding its Stamina maximum. A creature without a Stamina resource receives no secondary benefit.

source.originalText: Renewal: Healing Rites restore 5 stamina to the target.

cards.name: Flame
cards.rangeAndTarget: One creature damaged by your Smite or Rite
cards.frequency: At most once on each of your turns
cards.effect: Invocation Path — Flame. Tags: invocation, flame. Immediately after your Smite or Rite damages a creature, you may spend 1 Conviction. The target ignites and takes 1d6 fire damage at the start of each of its next 2 turns. Reapplying Flame refreshes the duration; the burning damage does not stack.

source.originalText: Flame: Conviction can be consumed to ignite targets for 2 turns (fire DoT).

cards.name: Veil
cards.frequency: Automatic only if Veil was selected
cards.effect: Invocation Path — Veil. Tags: invocation, veil, sight. You can see invisible and ethereal creatures and objects within 30 feet that are not behind total cover. This does not reveal mundane disguises, automatically defeat illusions, or let you see through opaque barriers.

source.originalText: Veil: Gain passive True Sight vs invisible or ethereal creatures.

cards.name: Echoes
cards.duration: Until start of your next regular turn
cards.frequency: At most one pending Echoes-path repeat
cards.effect: Invocation Path — Echoes. Tags: invocation, echoes. Once on each of your turns after a Smite or Rite produces rolled immediate damage or healing, store one original target and that raw dice total. At the start of your next regular turn, if the target is legal, repeat floor(raw dice total/10), minimum 1 for a positive total, as the same damage or healing type. This repeat carries no conditions, resources or triggers.

source.originalText: Echoes: 10% of healing or damage is repeated 1 turn later (Echo Effect).

cards.name: Divine Smite
cards.effect: Divine Smite. Tags: smite, divine. Make a Cleric technique attack against one enemy. On a hit, deal S d8 + M radiant damage. This is one damage event. Invocation Path bonuses and features explicitly referring to Smite may modify it.

source.originalText: Divine Smite: Channel divine energy into a powerful strike against a single enemy, dealing damage based on your Wisdom and consuming 1 Conviction.

cards.name: Healing Rite
cards.effect: Healing Rite. Tags: rite, healing. One living ally regains S d8 + M HP. It cannot restore a dead creature or remove Wounds. Consecrated Ground and appropriate Invocation Path bonuses may modify this healing.

source.originalText: Healing Rite: A channeled ability that restores health to an ally, with increased effectiveness on consecrated ground.

cards.name: Sacred Chant
cards.effect: Sacred Chant. Tags: chant, sustained, conviction. Pulse on start and once when maintained on each later regular turn with a Bonus Action. Under the base feature, the third pulse generates 1 Conviction. Only a real encounter can generate Conviction this way. Maintenance itself does not otherwise heal, damage or grant Conviction.

source.originalText: Sacred Chant: A sustained prayer that generates 1 Conviction every 3 turns while maintained.

cards.name: Consecrate
cards.rangeAndTarget: 15-foot-radius fixed zone centered at a point within 30 feet
cards.effect: Consecrate. Tags: rite, zone. Create sanctified terrain. Your Consecrated Ground feature recognizes this zone. Undead creatures in the zone have -1 on attack rolls. A creature leaving the zone loses that penalty immediately. Only one Consecrate zone created by you may exist at a time; creating another ends the first.

source.originalText: Consecrate: Sanctify the ground in a 15-foot radius, creating consecrated terrain that enhances your healing abilities and weakens undead enemies.

cards.name: Divine Insight
cards.rangeAndTarget: Self; subject matter concerning a religious matter, sacred location or divine presence
cards.effect: Divine Insight. Tags: ritual, information. Ask the Director one specific factual question about a religious practice, sacred location, divine presence or recognized supernatural sign available to your tradition. Receive one truthful fact, symbolic clue or 'unknown' if the information is genuinely unavailable. This never forces certainty about future events or another character's private beliefs.

source.originalText: Divine Insight: Commune briefly with your deity to gain insight about a religious matter, sacred location, or divine presence.

cards.name: Aura of Faith
cards.rangeAndTarget: Allies within 15 feet who can perceive you
cards.effect: Aura of Faith. Tags: aura, bishop. Allies in the aura gain +1 on saving throws. Whenever your Rite restores HP to an ally in the aura, that ally also regains 1 additional HP. Multiple Aura of Faith bonuses do not stack.

source.originalText: Aura of Faith: Allies in range gain +5% healing received and +1 to saves.

cards.name: Sermon of Purpose
cards.effect: Sermon of Purpose. Tags: chant, conviction, bishop. Sacred Chant generates its 1 Conviction on its second pulse instead of its third. A normal three-pulse Sacred Chant still generates only 1 Conviction total unless another feature explicitly extends it or grants an additional generation event.

source.originalText: Sermon of Purpose: Chants now generate 1 Conviction every 2 turns.

cards.name: Liturgical Flow
cards.effect: Liturgical Flow. Tags: rite, invocation, recharge. If you start Rites on two consecutive regular turns, your next Divine Invocation started before the end of your following regular turn sets its printed round-recharge counter 1 lower, minimum 0. This counts as Divine Invocation's one allowed reset or shortening for that round.

source.originalText: Liturgical Flow: Chaining 2 Rites reduces cooldown of your next Invocation by 1 turn.

cards.name: Anointed Guardian
cards.rangeAndTarget: First ally within 30 feet to fall to one-quarter maximum HP or less
cards.effect: Anointed Guardian. Tags: protection, bishop. The first qualifying ally in an encounter gains a ward for 2 rounds. The first time during each round that ally takes damage, reduce that damage by PB + M, minimum 0. The ward does not prevent conditions attached to an attack unless the damage reduction itself invalidates them under another rule.

source.originalText: Anointed Guardian: First time an ally drops below 20% HP per combat, grant them a 30% damage reduction shield for 2 rounds.

cards.name: Sanctified Reprisal
cards.duration: Until end of your next regular turn
cards.effect: Sanctified Reprisal. Tags: healing, smite, bishop. After one of your Cleric features restores HP to a living creature, empower your next Divine Smite before the end of your next regular turn. On a hit it deals S d4 additional radiant damage. If the target is Undead, it must also make a Constitution save; failure Stuns it until the end of its next turn.

source.originalText: Sanctified Reprisal: Whenever you heal, next Smite deals 20% more damage and stuns Undead.

cards.name: Miraculous Channel
cards.rangeAndTarget: Your next ally-targeting Rite this turn
cards.effect: Miraculous Channel. Tags: rite, channel, bishop. Your next Rite this turn that normally affects one or more willing allies may affect up to six legal willing allies within the Rite's normal range instead. Roll shared healing or numeric effects once and apply normally. It does not multiply hostile targets, corpse targets or resource generation.

source.originalText: Miraculous Channel: Sacrificing 3 Conviction causes your next Rite to affect the full party.

cards.name: Bishop's Mandate
cards.rangeAndTarget: Your Sacrament and one legal Divine Invocation target set
cards.frequency: Automatic at Cleric 9; once per Sacrament start
cards.effect: Bishop's Mandate. Tags: sacrament, invocation, capstone. When you legally start Sacrament, immediately resolve one free Divine Invocation using your selected Invocation Path. This free Invocation requires no Action, RP or Conviction, sets no Divine Invocation recharge and cannot itself trigger Bishop's Mandate. The Sacrament's own Conviction expenditure may still vent Dissonance normally.

source.originalText: Capstone: Bishop's Mandate: Activating a Sacrament automatically casts a free Invocation without cost or cooldown.

cards.name: Divine Invocation
cards.effect: Divine Invocation. Tags: invocation, bishop. Use only your selected Invocation Path. Radiance: up to 3 allies within 30 feet each regain S d8+M HP; one may end Frightened or Poisoned. Judgment: one enemy within 60 feet makes a Wisdom save, taking (S+1)d8 radiant on failure or half on success; failure also applies Judged for 2 rounds. Renewal: up to 2 allies within 30 feet each regain S d8+M HP and 5 Stamina. Flame: creatures in a 15-foot cone make Dexterity saves, taking (S+1)d8 fire on failure or half on success; failed targets also take 1d6 fire at the start of their next turn. Veil: up to 3 allies within 30 feet can see invisible/ethereal creatures within 30 feet and gain advantage on saves against illusions for 3 rounds. Echoes: choose one eligible Smite or Rite you resolved this turn or previous regular turn and one original target within 30 feet; repeat 50% of its immediate unmodified rolled damage or healing dice, rounded down once, minimum 1 for a positive source, with no copied conditions, resources or triggers.

source.originalText: Divine Invocation: Channel a powerful prayer based on your chosen Invocation Path, with effects ranging from mass healing to divine fire or protective barriers.

cards.name: Sacrament
cards.cost: 3 Conviction + 4 RP to start; 1 RP maintenance
cards.effect: Sacrament. Tags: sacrament, rite, sustained, zone. Pulse on start and on each paid Bonus Action maintenance. At each pulse, up to three allies in the zone gain +1 on saving throws until the start of your next regular turn or effect end, whichever is first. Up to three Undead or Fiends in the zone make Wisdom saves, taking S d6 radiant damage on failure or half on success. Maximum 3 pulses.

source.originalText: Sacrament: Perform a sacred ceremony that consumes Conviction to create a powerful, sustained effect in an area.

cards.name: Banish Unholy
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to three Undead or Fiends within 30 feet
cards.duration: Instantaneous; banishment rider lasts until end of target's next turn
cards.effect: Banish Unholy. Tags: divine, control. Each target makes a Wisdom save. Failure deals (S+1)d8 radiant damage and pushes it up to 15 feet directly away from you; success takes half damage and no push. A target failing by 10 or more is also banished until the end of its next turn, then returns to the nearest legal space.

source.originalText: Banish Unholy: Channel divine energy to damage and potentially banish undead, demons, or other unholy entities.

cards.name: Blessing of Protection
cards.effect: Blessing of Protection. Tags: blessing, protection. Choose one mode on use. Resistance: choose acid, cold, fire, lightning, necrotic, poison, radiant or thunder; the ally gains resistance to that damage type. Resolve: choose Charmed, Frightened or Poisoned; the ally gains advantage on saves against that condition and may immediately repeat one current save against it.

source.originalText: Blessing of Protection:  Bestow a divine blessing on an ally, granting them resistance to a specific damage type or condition.

cards.name: Commune
cards.effect: Commune. Tags: ritual, information, bishop. Ask up to three questions concerning divine doctrine, sacred duties, supernatural threats or a course of action. For each, the Director answers truthfully with yes, no, unclear or a brief symbolic response based on what the contacted divine source could know. Commune cannot compel a deity, reveal another player's private belief, or guarantee a future choice.

source.originalText: Commune:  Enter a deep meditative state to receive guidance directly from your deity, gaining insight on important matters or divine intervention.

cards.name: Aura of Grace
cards.frequency: Healing once/own regular turn; critical reduction once/ally/round
cards.effect: Aura of Grace. At the start of your regular turn during a real encounter, you may pay 1 RP to heal S HP to up to 3 living allies within 15 ft below half maximum HP. You must be conscious. Separately, once per ally per round when an ally in the aura suffers a critical hit, reduce its added critical damage by one damage die, minimum 0 extra dice. No unlimited free healing.

source.originalText: Aura of Grace: Allies in range resist critical hits and gain minor HP regen.

cards.name: Divine Rebirth
cards.rangeAndTarget: One ally revived by your Cleric feature
cards.duration: Instantaneous plus temporary HP for 1 minute
cards.effect: Divine Rebirth. Tags: saint, resurrection. When one of your Cleric features returns an ally from death, you may use Divine Rebirth. That ally returns with half its maximum HP instead of the feature's normal returned HP and gains S + M temporary HP for 1 minute. It removes no Wounds and cannot affect a creature that was not actually dead.

source.originalText: Divine Rebirth: On revive, ally returns with 50% HP and a temporary resistance shield.

cards.name: Merciful Sacrament
cards.effect: Merciful Sacrament. Tags: saint, sacrament. When you start Sacrament and at least one living ally inside its initial zone is at or below one-quarter maximum HP, you may reduce that Sacrament's Conviction cost to 0. Its RP cost and all other requirements remain. Because no Conviction is spent, this waived cost does not vent Dissonance.

source.originalText: Merciful Sacrament: Sacraments cost no Conviction if used on an ally under 25% HP.

cards.name: Unyielding Light
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to six living party members within 30 feet, including you
cards.effect: Unyielding Light. Tags: saint, emergency, healing. When one damage event would leave every conscious living party member within 30 feet at 0 HP, resolve that damage, then before ordinary death-save progression each qualifying living creature at 0 HP regains floor(maximum HP/3), minimum 1. It cannot revive a creature killed outright and removes no Wounds. This one emergency trigger may resolve even if that event incapacitates you, provided you remain alive; it grants no other actions while incapacitated.

source.originalText: Unyielding Light: Once per day, prevents party wipe and restores 30% HP.

cards.name: Celestial Resurgence
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to six allied corpses within 30 feet that died during the previous 3 rounds
cards.effect: Final Miracle — Celestial Resurgence. Tags: saint, finale, resurrection, rite. Each legal target returns to life at 1 HP. The body must be sufficiently present to sustain life. This removes no Wounds, curses or other death consequences. Divine Rebirth may modify one returned ally if available. The Conviction expenditure can vent Dissonance once under the common rule.

source.originalText: Final Miracle: Celestial Resurgence: Revive all allies who died within the last 3 turns.

cards.name: Mass Healing Light
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to six living allies within 30 feet
cards.effect: Mass Healing Light. Tags: saint, healing. Roll S d8 + M once. Each target regains that amount. A target below half maximum HP when chosen regains an additional 1d8 HP. Roll that bonus once and apply it to all qualifying targets. This cannot revive the dead or remove Wounds.

source.originalText: Mass Healing Light: Channel divine energy to heal all allies within 30 feet, with increased effectiveness on those most wounded.

cards.name: Divine Intervention
cards.effect: Divine Intervention. Tags: saint, emergency. Trigger when the ally either fails a saving throw or takes damage that would reduce it to 0 HP. Choose one: the ally rerolls the failed save and must use the new result; or reduce the triggering damage by 2 S d8 + M, minimum 0. This cannot negate an event that has already fully resolved.

source.originalText: Divine Intervention: Call upon your deity to intervene directly, potentially averting disaster or creating a miraculous effect.

cards.name: Sanctify Being
cards.effect: Sanctify Being. Tags: saint, protection. Choose one mode. Elemental Sanctity grants resistance to one of acid, cold, fire, lightning, necrotic, poison, radiant or thunder. Purity grants immunity to exactly one of Charmed, Frightened or Poisoned. Choose when activated; the choice cannot change during that use.

source.originalText: Sanctify Being: Bestow temporary divine protection on an ally, granting them immunity to specific conditions or damage types.

cards.name: Radiant Burst
cards.rangeAndTarget: 15-foot radius centered on you; up to six allies and six Undead/Fiends
cards.effect: Radiant Burst. Tags: saint, healing, radiant. Roll S d8 once. Each chosen living ally regains that roll + M HP. Each chosen Undead or Fiend makes a Wisdom save, taking the same S d8 roll as radiant damage on failure or half on success. Healing and damage are separate applications of the shared roll.

source.originalText: Radiant Burst: Release a powerful wave of divine energy that heals allies and damages unholy creatures.

cards.name: Resurrection
cards.rangeAndTarget: One allied corpse you touch that died within the previous 1 minute
cards.effect: Resurrection. Tags: saint, resurrection, rite. Return the target to life at 1 HP and grant it 2 S + M temporary HP for 1 minute. It gains no removed Wounds and receives no restored expended resources beyond what another rule explicitly provides. A missing vital body prevents the effect. The Conviction expenditure can vent Dissonance once.

source.originalText: Resurrection: Return a fallen ally to life with renewed vigor and temporary divine blessing.

cards.name: Scriptural Echo
cards.rangeAndTarget: One legal original target of your previously used Divine Invocation
cards.effect: Scriptural Echo. Tags: priest, rite, invocation. When you start a Rite, you may repeat 50% of the immediate rolled damage or healing dice from the most recent Divine Invocation you personally resolved since the end of your previous regular turn. Round down once, minimum 1 for a positive source. It copies no conditions, movement, resource effects, control or Invocation Path triggers.

source.originalText: Scriptural Echo: Casting a Rite repeats the Invocation used previously for 50% effect.

cards.name: Words of Equilibrium
cards.effect: Words of Equilibrium. Tags: priest, scaling. For numeric Cleric technique healing and damage that would add your Wisdom modifier, use the higher of your Intelligence or Wisdom modifier instead. M becomes max(1, that higher modifier) for those numeric effects. This does not change Cleric attack rolls or save DCs unless another rule explicitly says so.

source.originalText: Words of Equilibrium: Heal and Damage dealt scale off the higher of INT or WIS.

cards.name: Balanced Scales
cards.rangeAndTarget: Living creatures healed by your Cleric features
cards.duration: Until start of your next regular turn
cards.frequency: At most once per marked ally per round
cards.effect: Balanced Scales. Tags: priest, healing, retaliation. After you restore HP to a living ally, mark it until the start of your next regular turn. The first enemy to damage that ally during the mark takes S + M radiant damage. The retaliation is not an attack, cannot critically hit and cannot recursively trigger another Balanced Scales event.

source.originalText: Balanced Scales: Enemies take divine damage if they attack healed targets.

cards.name: Doctrine Shield
cards.effect: Doctrine Shield. Tags: priest, conviction, cleanse. During a real encounter, when one of your Cleric features successfully removes Charmed, Frightened, Poisoned or another explicitly removable condition from a living creature, gain 1 Conviction. Removing multiple conditions in the same event still grants only 1 Conviction.

source.originalText: Doctrine Shield: Gain 1 Conviction anytime a condition is removed.

cards.name: Word of Binding
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to six enemies within 30 feet
cards.effect: Final Miracle — Word of Binding. Tags: priest, finale, control, rite. Each target makes a Wisdom save. On failure it is Silenced and its Speed becomes 0. At the end of each of its turns it repeats the save, ending both effects on success. While a target remains bound, the first instance of divine or radiant damage it takes each round gains S d6 additional radiant damage. The Conviction expenditure can vent Dissonance once.

source.originalText: Final Miracle: Word of Binding: Enemies in a large AoE are silenced, snared, and take +25% divine damage for 3 turns.

cards.name: Balance Restoration
cards.rangeAndTarget: 15-foot-radius area centered at a point within 30 feet
cards.effect: Balance Restoration. Tags: priest, healing, radiant. Choose up to three living allies and three enemies in the area. Roll S d8 once. Each ally regains the roll + M HP. Each enemy makes a Wisdom save, taking the same S d8 roll as radiant damage on failure or half on success.

source.originalText: Balance Restoration: Channel divine energy that both heals allies and damages enemies in an area, maintaining cosmic balance.

cards.name: Divine Judgment
cards.effect: Divine Judgment. Tags: priest, judgment. The target makes a Wisdom save; success ends the attempt. On failure it is marked. The first time on each of its turns that it deals damage to another creature, it takes radiant damage equal to half that actual damage rounded down, minimum 1, maximum your Cleric level. It repeats the Wisdom save at the end of each turn, ending the mark on success.

source.originalText: Divine Judgment: Mark an enemy for judgment, causing them to take damage proportional to the harm they inflict.

cards.name: Ritual of Cleansing
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to three living allies within 30 feet; secondary enemies within 15 feet of you
cards.effect: Ritual of Cleansing. Tags: priest, rite, cleanse. Each ally may end one of Charmed, Frightened or Poisoned. For each distinct condition actually removed, choose one enemy within 15 feet; each chosen enemy makes a Wisdom save. On failure it becomes Frightened of you until the end of its next turn. One enemy can be chosen only once per use.

source.originalText: Ritual of Cleansing: Perform a ritual that removes multiple negative conditions from allies while potentially imposing them on enemies.

cards.name: Word of Power
cards.effect: Word of Power. Tags: priest, divine. Choose one mode. Mercy: one willing living creature regains S d8+M HP. Rebuke: one Undead or Fiend makes a Constitution save, taking (S+1)d8 radiant on failure or half on success; failure also removes its Reaction until the start of its next turn. Command: one other hostile creature makes a Wisdom save; failure knocks it Prone and removes its Reaction until the start of its next turn. No mode changes beliefs, loyalty or ideology.

source.originalText: Word of Power: Speak a divine word that has different effects based on the target's nature and actions.

cards.name: Cosmic Equilibrium
cards.effect: Cosmic Equilibrium. Tags: priest, zone, healing, radiant. Once per round, when a living ally in the zone receives healing beyond its missing HP, redirect up to S+M of that excess as radiant damage to one enemy in the zone.
